title: an as-observed register row differs from v2 behaviour and every existing check passes, because nothing compares an as-observed claim to what the command actually does
body:
**`agent_commands.bats` is classified `keep` / `as-observed` in the parity register and it FAILS, because v3 does not reproduce what v2 was measured doing.** The row's disposition asserts that it does.

=== THE DEVIATION, DRIVEN ===

    tests/unit/agent_commands.bats:71  @test "claude subagents command shows help when no subcommand given"
      run run_intent claude subagents
      assert_success
      assert_output_contains "Usage: intent claude subagents <command>"

    v3:  error: 'intent claude subagents' requires a subcommand but one was not provided

v2 printed usage and exited 0. v3 refuses and exits non-zero. The COMMAND is present and correct -- `intent claude subagents --help` answers `Manage Claude Code subagents` -- so the register and the binary agree on SHAPE and disagree on BEHAVIOUR.

=== WHY IT WAS SILENT, WHICH IS THE PART THAT GENERALISES ===

**No instrument checks an `as-observed` claim against behaviour.** `implemented_check.sh`'s own header already records that the surface instruments compare the table to the binary's SHAPE, and that the register cannot distinguish WIRED from WIRED-AND-IMPLEMENTED. This is the third gap on that same line: it cannot distinguish IMPLEMENTED from BEHAVES-AS-V2 either.

Every existing check passes on this row. The command exists, the table declares it, the shapes agree. The only thing that disagrees is what it DOES, and nothing asks.

=== A WRONG CAUSE WAS PROPOSED FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT ===

cc first attributed the failure to `intent claude subagents` having been PRUNED, evidenced by the deletion of `intent/plugins/claude/bin/intent_claude_subagents` (742 lines) at `125f601d` under AC-12.1. **That deletion is real and it is NOT this failure's cause.** It is the v2 plugin SCRIPT; the v3 command is built in and answers. The error cc generalised from came from a DIFFERENT test in the same file (line 760, which invokes the plugin path directly), selected by a grep that took the first matching error line in the file's output and reported it as the file's cause.

**The wrong cause implied a damaging repair**: moving the row to `retire` would have deleted a SHIPPING command from the register and created the divergence in the opposite direction. Caught by vc driving the binary rather than reading the report.

=== SCOPE ===

The concrete deviation is this issue. **Whether a behaviour-level register check is built in this cut is NOT decided here** -- it is new surface in a tag window, it is hv's call, and vc has put it to them.

Filed because ST0056 `AC-06.3`, as reworded by vc's ruling on 2026-08-31, requires that a `keep`/`as-observed` row found to differ from v2's measured behaviour is a recorded deviation or a filed defect, **never silence**. This is the filing.
